chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:
For ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah and for wudu (ablution), that amount is sufficient of it which is sufficient of oil that moistens the body.

key_terms.الدُّهْنِ: oil, used here as a comparison for how lightly something may cover the body
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl (ritual bath), here referring to purification from janābah
key_terms.يُجْزِي: is sufficient; fulfills the required minimum

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of water sufficient for ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah and wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal measure for the minimum amount of water sufficient in ghusl (ritual bath) from janābah and in wudu (ablution). The criterion given is an amount that reaches and moistens the body, like oil that spreads over it.
